rationale: Fourteenth turn: the cluster harness gains a reconfiguration case on the authority-transition axis - a StopSign is proposed while one participant is down, the live participants must report being stopped and must reject further proposals, and the participant that missed the reconfiguration must learn the decided StopSign after recovery. The case ran locally with all three properties holding, so the run is requested to record reconfiguration and its propagation in a retained receipt; the three earlier cases (stale-decided recovery, batched mixed proposals, leader change plus recovery) still run in the same target but their comparisons were already evaluated in the preceding revision and are not redeclared here.

scope.description: One added deterministic in-process case over real OmniPaxos instances: with a four-entry prefix already decided, one participant is removed, the leader proposes the next configuration (configuration_id 2), the harness waits until every live participant reports is_reconfigured() with a StopSign, checks that a further append is rejected, then rebuilds the removed participant from its persisted storage and waits until it also reports the decided StopSign and has caught up to the leader's decided index.
assumptions: Three nodes, pids {1,2,3}, configuration_id 1, majority quorum, batch_size 2, deterministic message routing; the next configuration lists the same pids with configuration_id 2.

Removing a participant is modelled by dropping its instance while keeping its storage handle; recovery rebuilds the instance from that handle, so the recovered node repromises with the promise it had persisted.
The StopSign decision therefore needs only the two live participants (the majority), matching the environment assumption that one of three participants is unavailable.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled, as in every run of this session.
excluded: The new configuration itself is not instantiated: only the stopping protocol of the current one is exercised.
No participant is added, removed or replaced by the new configuration, and no message loss beyond the one removed participant is applied.
Snapshot and persistent backend variants are not exercised by this case.

experiment.prefix: Cluster::new(3, 2) builds OmniPaxos instances over shared in-memory storage handles and pump_until ticks and routes until a (Leader, Accept) exists; the harness appends TestEntry(0..4) on the leader and pump_until every node reports decided_idx 4, then emits reconfig_admitted with the leader, the participant to be removed and the prefix length. It removes that participant from the cluster, calls reconfigure(ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 2, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None }, None) on the leader, and pump_until both live participants report is_reconfigured() == Some, after which it calls append(TestEntry(999)) on the leader and records whether that call was rejected; both observations are emitted in case_result_reconfig_live. Finally it rebuilds the removed participant from its storage handle and pump_until it reports is_reconfigured() == Some and its decided index is at least the leader's, emitting case_result_reconfig_recovered.
semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the case uses only public API calls (reconfigure, is_reconfigured, append, get_decided_idx).
experiment.responsibility: Under test is the current configuration's stopping protocol and the propagation of the decided StopSign to a participant that was absent while it was reached, i.e. the participants' transition out of eligibility and the obligation to complete the reconfiguration for a returning participant.

comparisons.description: Both live participants report the decided StopSign once the leader has proposed the next configuration.
A further proposal on the stopped configuration is rejected rather than accepted.
The participant that was absent when the StopSign was decided learns it after recovery and catches up to the leader's decided index.

experiment.revision_reason: Reconfiguration case added to the same cluster harness to cover the authority-transition axis (StopSign decision with one participant down, rejection of further proposals, and propagation to the recovered participant). The previously declared cases remain in the harness and in the fixed artifact; their comparisons were evaluated in the preceding revision.
